description_en: Mū Bāhāḥ is located behind theaśoka caityato the west of Piṃbāhāl. The Bāhāḥ can be accessed via a newly constructed gate with two openings. The outer gate of the Bāhāḥ is made from iron rods. The courtyard measures 14.25m x 14.25m and is paved withteliatiles. It is also home to avajradhātu caitya(1.6m high), which sits at its centre, and a plasteredcaitya(1.85m high). The main three-storey shrine building (thedyaḥchẽ)is facing east. The front façade of the building is plastered withlivã(grey sandy clay + cow dung + rice husk) and white-washed with lime, but the ground floor plaster has already deteriorated due to damp rising from the ground. The ground floor is furnished with a central main carved door with lattice door leafs. This in turn is flanked by two small lattice windows (tikijhhyā). Some traces of paintings of Buddha images can be seen on the plaster on top of the door head. The end walls of the buildings (kilāsa) have pilasters of the same height with decorative floral design on the floor cornice levels. The first floor has apāsukā jhyāwith three openings at the centre and a latticed window on either side. The second floor has a large three-bay window. Its central opening is rectangular while the two side openings are arched. The upper floor can be accessed via the annex building to the north through a single door (see map). The first floor of this block is furnished with a lattice window and the second floor contains a single open arched window. The gable roof of the building is covered with small tiles. The southern end wall has been reconstructed but is still in a critical condition due to damage suffered by the earthquake and rain.At the southern side of the courtyard is a three storieddigichẽ.This building has similar architecture to thedyaḥchẽbuilding but is more decorated. The ground floor is furnished with a central main carved wooden door with carvings of wisdom bearers on the lintel ends. There are three Buddha images on the head of the main door, which is flanked with small lattice windows on either side. The plasterwork has deteriorated due to the damp. The inside bay of the building is colonnaded on the ground floor to the south, and the floors are separated from one another by well-carved wooden cornices which cannot be found in thedyaḥchẽ. The first floor is even more embellished withpāsukā jhyāwith five openings flanked by two aedicules and two blind windows on either side. The central opening of thepasukā jhyāis emphasised by thetoraṇa thã. However, thetoraṇaseems to be missing. The second floor is readily visible with the joist ends protruding out of the wall. This floor is an open colonnaded space which is used for feasts andpujaactivities and is furnished with a large three-bay window with two single-bay windows on either side. All of the openings of this building are rectangular in shape. Thedigichẽcan be accessed via an annex building to the right on the west side. This annex building has a main carved door frame with plain lintel ends on its ground floor. Its first floor has a well carvedpasukā jhyāwith three openings which is flanked by two small blind windows. The second floor has a big window with vertical timber battens. The annex building's walls are of exposed brick, and the western end wall collapsed due to an earthquake.Mū Bāhāḥ is a major location among the branches of the Hiraṇyavarṇa Mahāvihāra, and it is for this reason that it is known as Mū (‘main’) Bāhāḥ.Members of this Bāhāḥhave been managing daily and other ritual worships, and taking care of theaśoka caityasituated nearby. There is a customary practice that thethapāḥāḥjuof this Bāhāḥ purifies the worshipping altar by making an offering of water during the Ilhane Samyak festival of the Nāga Bāhāḥ.
description_ne: यो विहार पिंबहाल टोलमा रहेको ठूलो अशोक स्तूप (चिलंद्य:) को पछाडि अवस्थित छ । यो हिरण्यवर्ण महाविहार, क्वा:बहा:को शाखा विहार हो । हिरण्यवर्ण महाविहारका शाखा विहारहरूमध्ये मुख्य शाखा विहार भएकोले यसलाई मूबहा: भनिएको हो । विहारमा प्रवेश गर्ने मूलद्वार फलामको रेलिङ्ग राखी बनाइएको छ । मूलद्वारको ठीक सामुन्ने तीनतलाको द्य:छेँ रहेको छ । द्य:छेँको छाना झिंगटीले छाएको छ । छानामाथि कुनै गजूर वा चैत्य राखिएको छैन । छाना अड्याउन सादा टुँडाल प्रयोग गरिएका छन् । द्य:छेँको दोस्रो तलामा तीनवटा ठूला झ्यालहरू राखिएका छन् । पहिलो तलामा त्रिखा झ्याल राखी दायाँ-बायाँ एक-एक वटा साना झ्याल राखिएका छन् । भुइँतलामा विहारको गर्भगृह रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पस्ने ढोकाको माथि कुनै तोरण राखिएको छैन । गर्भगृहको दायाँ-बायाँ सिंह र घण्टा पनि राखिएका छैनन् । गर्भगृहभित्र पृर्वाभिमुख गरी अक्षोभ्य बुद्धलाई क्वा:पा:द्य:को रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ ।विहार परिसरमा दुईवटा चैत्य रहेका छन् । दक्षिणपट्टि विहारको दिगिछेँ रहेको छ । त्यसै दिगिछेँमा विहारको आगम पनि रहेको छ । वर्षातको पानीले गर्दा भूकम्पले जीर्ण भैसकेको यो दिगिछेँको पश्चिमी भाग भत्किएको छ ।विहारसँगै रहेको अशोक चैत्य (चिलंद्य:)को हेरचाह, नित्यपूजाका साथै धार्मिक क्रियाकलाप पनि यसै विहारबाट संचालन भैरहेका छन् । नागबहालमा मनाइने इल्हने सम्यक्‌मा यस विहारका थपा:आ:जुले जलधारा अर्पण गरी भूमिशोधन गर्नुपर्ने परम्परा छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Consecration of image of wooden Vajrasattva
historical_events.event_description: During the reign of King Yakṣa Malla, the Mahāpātras of the Piṃ Bāhāla area of Patan performed a great fire worship (yajña) and established a wooden image of Vajrasattva Tathāgata. On the same occasion they offered a bronze image of the moon, two bells and abhṛṅgāra. However, the image of the Vajrasattva kept inside the sanctum of the Bāhāḥ has since been stolen.
